text: rwb-case keeps GET /cases and GET /cases/export as the system-of-record read and its own export, and rwb-integration adds a read-only composed page on GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/case-list and an Excel export on GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/case-list/export for the integration slice of this legacy key; the same page is composed twice, and the duplication is stated in both stories.
why: The Ownership Map keeps GET /cases and GET /cases/export with P3 and ADR-020 with DP-19 puts SCR-02 on the owner service, while the WP splits a P2 APP slice that owns AC1 to AC11; the conflict is resolved the way RWB-P2-E2006-APP resolved its double composition, by recording it.
read: Ownership Map API GET /cases and GET /cases/export (owner P3); Architecture v5 slides 13, 14, 41 and 45; Template and Rules v1 §R3; RWB-P2-E2006-APP section 2.
applied_in: §1 Story, §2 Business rationale, §7 AC note, §8 BR9, §12.1 REST provided, §19 Out of scope
confirm: Solution architect; the rwb-case owner (RWB-P3-E1031-CON and RWB-P3-E2033-APP)
impact: Two read surfaces over one set of owner contracts; the case-side answer stays the record and both are tested against each other.

text: The two composed operations sit on the service base /api/recovery/integration/v1 under DP-13 as /case-list and /case-list/export; they are not rows of the Ownership Map, so their exact form is fixed at the contract review of RWB-P2-E2033-CON and is not derived from another service's path.
why: The Ownership Map keeps GET /cases and GET /cases/export with P3 and no source names a case-list path on the integration base, so the path is a gap and not a copy.
read: Ownership Map API; Architecture v5 slides 14, 16 and 41; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-13 and §R9.
confirm: Solution architect; platform API catalogue owner
impact: The app story and the screen call the two paths of this contract; a change of path is a contract change and not a code change.

text: rwb-integration runs as its own ACE database login with grants on its own schema only (DP-02), replacing the legacy shared recovery_svc identity; the login follows the rwb_integration schema name of Architecture v5 slide 29 and holds no grant on the recovery schema or on another rwb_* schema.
why: No source document names the per-service login, while DP-02 requires one login per service and Architecture v5 slide 29 shows one login per schema.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 29 and 41; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-02; legacy RWB-E2-033 section 10.
confirm: ACE team, DBA (schema and login provisioning, RWB-PLT-DB)
impact: The story builds and tests against the rwb-integration login once it is allocated; no behaviour of the read changes.

text: The page answer carries the rows of the caller's scope with the paging envelope of the legacy page and the twelve columns caseNo, product, queue, owner, status, stage, ageDays, serviceLevelState, serviceLevelDueAt, prescriptionDate, prescriptionClockStatus and deviationOpen, and every error is returned as the platform problem body with its message identifier; the JSON field names and the problem body shape are fixed at the contract review.
why: The sources name the legacy response type of the page and the twelve columns, not the JSON names of the composed answer, the filter set or the problem body.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-033 sections 4, 7 and 12; Architecture v5 slide 11 (problem details); Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 s12.
applied_in: §11 Data, §12.1 REST provided, §14 Validation and messages
impact: The names are fixed once in the baseline and consumed by the app story and the test stories; no behaviour of the read changes.

text: The ageing and service-level read of rwb-case (RWB-P3-E2011-CON) publishes ageDays, stageClockStart, serviceLevelDueAt, serviceLevelState, prescriptionDate and prescriptionClockStatus for a page of case ids, batched so that one composed page is one hop; the per-case timer projection GET /cases/{caseId}/timers of the Ownership Map is not called once per row.
why: A per-case read of the timer projection would put one call per row inside one page and break the one-hop, 2 s budget of ADR-020, while the legacy story read the timer rows for the whole page in one query.
read: Ownership Map API GET /cases/{caseId}/timers and tables timer (owner P3); Architecture v5 slides 14, 41 and 45; legacy RWB-E2-033 flow step 5 and section 11.
applied_in: §4 Flow, §11 Data, §12.2 REST consumed, §13 Solution plan
impact: One batched read per page instead of one per case; the field names are fixed in the P3 contract story.

text: caselist.export.maxrows stays 10,000 as the legacy story assumes under DL11 and the case-list page bounds stay 1 and 200, and both become rows of the rwb-case parameter contract with the version in force; no limit is written in code or in the contract as a constant.
why: The legacy story marks the export limit as assumed and reads the page size bounds as a validation rule, while DP-06 and the legacy guardrail require every changeable value to be a parameter row.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-033 section 3, AC7, AC10, BR7 and section 13; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-06; Ownership Map parameter_catalog and parameter_value (owner P3) and API GET /admin/parameters.
applied_in: §3 Preconditions, §8 BR7 and BR10, §12.2 REST consumed, §13 Configuration and reference data
confirm: Business lead for the export limit; the rwb-case parameter owner (RWB-P3-E1042-CON)
impact: The export limit and the page bounds are data rows; a change of limit is a data change and no release.

text: LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE are read as reference rows of rwb-case through the reference-data contract with the version in force, and the queue codes in force are read through the rwb-case queue list; the reference-data read path is fixed in RWB-P3-E1043-CON because no source names it.
why: DP-07 moves reference data and lists of values to rwb-case, the legacy story named the lists and the queues table only, and the Ownership Map carries no reference-data GET row.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-033 section 8 BR6 and section 13; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-07 and §R3 default rulings; Ownership Map lov_value and reference_row (owner P3).
applied_in: §11 Data, §12.2 REST consumed, §13 Configuration and reference data
impact: Adding a value to a list is a data change in rwb-case and no code change here.

text: The export records exactly one access-log entry, through an operation of the rwb-access contract, before the file is made, and a refused entry produces no file; the path and the row shape of that operation are fixed in RWB-P4-E1037-CON because no source names them.
why: The access log is a row of rwb-access (Architecture v5 slide 41) while the legacy story writes it through the RWB-E1-039 interface of the monolith, and Architecture v5 slide 14 lists no access-log operation for rwb-access.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; Ownership Map tables (role, permission; the access log is P4's); legacy RWB-E2-033 section 12 and BR7; REQ-ACA-006.
applied_in: §4 Flow, §9 State transitions, §12.2 REST consumed, §13 Solution plan
impact: No access-log table exists in rwb_integration; the entry is the owner's row and a refused entry fails the export.

text: SCR-02 Case list is served by the gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the route path, the screen-model field list and the merge order are that platform story's to fix.
why: DP-19 puts every screen behind the gateway-bff composite route and no source fixes the route of this screen.
read: Architecture v5 slides 8, 10 and 20; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-19; legacy RWB-E2-033 section 15.
applied_in: §4 Flow, §12.8 Contract fakes, §15 Screens and states
impact: The screen is built against the composite-route stub and the route is agreed in the platform story; the two operations are unchanged.

text: This story adds no table and no migration: the composed read copies nothing into rwb_integration and writes no library row, so DP-15 applies to the service baseline only and RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is a build dependency for the migration conventions, not for a migration of this story.
why: DP-15 is in the pattern list of the legacy key, while the legacy story writes no business row and the Ownership Map lists no P2 table for the case list.
read: Ownership Map tables (interface_config, outbound_item, job_catalog under P2; the four library objects under PLT); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-15; legacy RWB-E2-033 section 9 and section 13.
applied_in: §12.7 Tables owned, §13 Solution plan (database and migrations)
impact: No schema change and no Flyway file; the rwb_integration baseline is carried by RWB-P2-E1007-APP.

text: This slice publishes no event and adds no event name: the topic rwb.integration.events.v1 carries only FileDelivered and FileFailed from the file stories of the service, and DP-14 applies to the names of the service and not to a new event here.
why: DP-14 is in the pattern list of the legacy key while the legacy story publishes nothing and Architecture v5 slides 16 and 43 give the service exactly two events, both on the outbound file side.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 42 and 43; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-14; legacy RWB-E2-033 section 12.
impact: The topic and its two events stay as the file stories define them; this story adds no subscription and no producer.

text: The legacy flag rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing stays the name of the switch, and the switch itself is a feature flag of the platform flag library read by rwb-integration (R-PREC default ruling; the Ownership Map gives feature_flag to PLT), not a row of a Workbench table; off ignores the breached parameter and serves the case-side columns only.
why: Feature flags belong to the platform library by the default ruling, while the legacy story reads the switch from the case module's own configuration and TSD P2 v3 defines feature_flag in rwb_integration.
read: Template and Rules v1 §R3 default rulings; Ownership Map feature_flag (owner PLT); TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 and API-P2-005 to API-P2-008; legacy RWB-E2-033 section 3 and section 13.
impact: The flag value comes from the library; the legacy name is kept so the switch stays traceable to the legacy story.

text: The ageing and service-level rules of BR2 to BR5 are evaluated twice on the same owner fields: by the P3 ageing contract for the case-side screen and by AgeingAndBreachCalculator in rwb-integration for the composed page and the export; the case-side answer is the record and the composed answer is the composition, and the two are tested against each other.
why: The legacy story computed the values in the same module that read them, while the split puts the owner's computation case-side and still needs a local computation here to apply the breach filter and the order over one page.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-033 section 5 and BR2 to BR5; Ownership Map tables timer (owner P3) and API GET /cases/{caseId}/timers; Architecture v5 slide 41.
applied_in: §1 Story, §2 Business rationale, §7 AC note, §8 BR13, §13 Components
impact: One set of rules implemented twice; a change of a rule is a change in both stories and one shared test proves they agree.

text: The export is an Excel file produced on request from the composed rows and is never written to a data lake: the data lake is removed (DP-17, Architecture v5 slide 37), so REQ-ACA-006 is carried by the export access-log entry alone and no lake copy exists.
why: The legacy requirement REQ-ACA-006 names a data lake copy, while Architecture v5 slide 37 and DP-17 remove the data lake and the legacy story writes a file on request only.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16 and 37; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-17; legacy RWB-E2-033 flow step 9 and section 12; Program BRD REQ-ACA-006.
applied_in: §8 BR11, §12.3 Events published, §12.9 Call-type summary, §18 Traceability
confirm: Solution architect; Data steward for the retention of the file
impact: One file per export with no stored copy and no lake path; the retention of the download is the environment's file handling.

text: The queue codes in force, their team code and their role are read through the rwb-case queue list (the Ownership Map row GET /queues under the service base of DP-13) and not from a queue table of this service; the legacy queues table of RWB-E1-019 is rwb-case's row store and is never read here.
why: The legacy story validated the queue filter against a queues table it could read in one schema, while DP-01 and the Ownership Map give queue to rwb-case.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-033 section 3, section 8 BR6 and section 11; Ownership Map tables queue (owner P3) and API GET /queues; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-01.
impact: Adding or retiring a queue is a data change in rwb-case; the filter validates against the owner's list.
